# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- This item was already sufficiently defined; no interview questions were asked. The description, scope, and acceptance criteria were clear and actionable.

## Dependency & audit resolution (2026-10-01)

Producer confirmed the Steamworks backend registration (AC2) is not yet done and requires a dependency chain. Two dependency items were created in the core project (CG store — the correct home for Steamworks backend work; worklog does not support cross-store dependency edges, so they are recorded here as cross-project references):

- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine
- **CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1** — Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend *(depends on CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ)*

**AC2 therefore remains unmet until CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1 completes.** This item carries the `do-not-delegate` tag while externally blocked so the downtime worker does not re-dispatch it.

**Merge state:** the item's work is integrated into `dev`/`origin/dev` as commit `dd11ea4` (core → `d2d1f322`). The stale feature branch (which referenced the superseded core commit `4a287d4`) was reset to `dd11ea4`.

**AC4 call:** the drift guard requires the parent challenge-side mapping from **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** (which depends on this item, so no cycle is possible). AC4 is verified at parent integration time; the mapping is present uncommitted in the working tree today and will pass permanently once the parent lands.

## Plan review — 2026-11-05 (verified state)

Verified against the current checkout: main-street `dev` at `f4f083ed`, `core` submodule pinned at `5a16c2fb`, superproject working tree clean.

- **AC1 met** — `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains `achievementId: serial-seller` with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false` (13 entries in total).
- **AC3 met** — the `core` pointer now pins `5a16c2fb`, later than the `d2d1f322` recorded above, and that commit contains the manifest entry.
- **AC4 preconditions satisfied** — the parent mapping (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J) is now **committed**, not uncommitted as stated above: `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps all 13 challenges, and the manifest and the game-side mapping agree exactly (13 ↔ 13, no drift in either direction). `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` is the guard that exercises this.
- **AC2 unmet / external** — unchanged: blocked on `CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1` (Steamworks backend registration). Not verifiable from the repository.
- **AC5** — no documentation change beyond the manifest entry was identified as required; the existing 12-achievement pattern is followed.
- **AC6** — enforced by the dev-push gate; not re-run by this planning session.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-05 — Plan re-run (effort Extra Small / Low, so decomposition skipped): six review stages run, AC coverage 100% (proceed), stage set to `plan_complete`. Recorded the verified AC state above; no child work items created.

# Intake brief: Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** low · **Cross-repo:** yes (Tableau-Card-Engine core via the `./core` submodule) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL

## Problem statement

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declares two npm scripts — `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` — that point at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, a file that does **not** exist in a game repo (Option C: game repos have no root `scripts/` tree; the scaffold lives in the core at `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`). Invoking either script fails with a module-not-found error. The working game-repo entry point, `npm run scaffold`, passes `--core-root ./core` and exists in every generated repo.

Root cause (resolved): `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherits the **entire** core `scripts` map from the core manifest (line ~280: `...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(manifest.scripts ?? {}))`). `core/package.json` legitimately declares `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` for core-repo use, so both leak unmodified into every generated game repo. The description's open "which is true" question is answered: the template **does** emit them, but only by inheritance — the fix is a template-side filter, not merely deleting two lines from each repo.

## Users

- **Game-repo maintainers (agents and humans)** — run npm scripts inside a game repo without tripping over dead entries.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold:game` to either work or not be declared, so a script listed in my repo never fails with module-not-found."
- **Core scaffold owners (Tableau-Card-Engine)** — keep the template emitting only what a game repo can actually run.
  - *User story:* "As a core template owner, I want the scaffold to filter core-only scripts (including any future ones) out of generated repos, so a re-scaffold never reintroduces broken entries."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **This repo's `package.json` no longer declares `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games`.** `npm run scaffold` remains and resolves to `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street ...`. Guarded by a regression test (new `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`) asserting the two broken keys are absent and every `scaffold*` script's target file exists.
2. **The scaffold template stops emitting them.** `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` filters the core-only `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` entries out of the inherited scripts map. Add a unit test in `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` whose manifest declares both keys and asserts the rendered `package.json` omits them, so a re-scaffold cannot reintroduce them (AC2 of the original item).
3. **The core change is delivered.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` + its test land in Tableau-Card-Engine (CG work item, per the MS↔CG pairing precedent of MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED↔CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q); this repo records the engine commit via its `./core` submodule pointer bump (`npm run engine:sync`), and `npm run scaffold` on a fixture checkout regenerates a `package.json` without the two keys.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` documents `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo scaffold entry point and states that `scaffold:game(s)` are core-checkout-only commands; no game-repo-context doc references `scaffold:game(s)`. Core docs that use them (DEVELOPER.md, dev/creating-a-new-game.md, dev/multi-repo-architecture.md) are core-checkout context and remain accurate; a one-line "run from the core checkout" clarification is made where ambiguity exists.

# Finish gate: a lagging engine pin can fail the build itself when `engine:sync` advances past a breaking engine API change

Discovered during **MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4** (AC1 verification of **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6**), while reproducing the lagging-pin condition. Verification only: nothing was worked around; this item records the gap.

## What happens

`implement.py finish` runs `npm run build`, which starts with `engine:sync`. When the worktree's committed pin lags the engine tracked tip, `engine:sync` advances `./core` to the tip **before** `tsc --noEmit` / `vite build` run — so the build compiles the item's source against an engine the source was never written for.

Reproduced on a throwaway worktree at `a6ef0b7d` (pinned `21bedf7a`; engine `dev` tip `2305f888`), which still uses the pre-rename `hasChoices` manifest flag:

```
engine:sync: core updated 21bedf7a8c → 2305f888d0
src/MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.ts(88,5): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'hasChoices' does not exist in type 'ContentFieldMapping'.
tests/main-street/MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.test.ts(194,44): error TS2551: Property 'hasChoices' does not exist on type 'ManifestNode'. Did you mean 'isChoice'?
npm run build → exit 2
```

The build-churn exclusion (`SA-0MVZE164P0048306`) cannot help: it runs **after** a successful build. The same probe at `99489ad8` (pin still `21bedf7a`, but source already at `isChoice`) built cleanly and the exclusion worked as designed.

## Why it matters

The parent epic's user story is that a documentation- or evidence-only item must not be blocked by an unrelated engine bump. Today the re-pin no longer reaches the commit, but the build still runs against the advanced engine first, so an older worktree can fail to build for a reason the item never caused — and the failure arrives as a plain build error, not as an engine-composition condition.

## Options (not decided here)

- (A) Report the condition explicitly: when the pre-build pin lags the engine tip, record it in the finish report and the build-failure message ("build ran against engine <tip>, item pinned <sha> — the advance is not part of the commit"), so the operator can tell an engine-induced build failure from a source failure.
- (B) Build against the pinned composition: restore the pin/gitlink *before* the build and re-sync only when the item itself changes composition (needs producer sign-off — it touches the pin policy `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`).
- (C) Leave as-is and document it as an accepted limitation of syncing at build time.

Option (B) is the closest to remedy C (verify-only `engine:sync`), which the producer already rejected for the finish gate, so it must not be adopted silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The condition "pre-build pin lags the engine tracked tip and the build failed" is visible in the finish report and the build-failure comment, naming both SHAs.
- [ ] A published limitation note exists in `docs/dev/testing.md` / the implement skill reference if the behaviour is kept.
- [ ] No cache-key or pin-policy change without producer sign-off.

## Plan decision (2026-11-03)

**Option (A) adopted — keep the build-time sync, make the condition explicit — together with the documentation half of Option (C).** The item's own draft AC1 requires exactly this (both SHAs in the finish report *and* the build-failure comment), and AC3 forbids a cache-key or pin-policy change without sign-off. **Option (B) is explicitly not adopted:** it changes build composition and touches pin policy `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`, so it requires producer sign-off and must not be implemented as a side effect of this bug.

Assumptions recorded (not invented requirements):

- **Repository boundary (precedent Q1=A on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`):** the finish report and the build-failure comment are produced by `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` in **SorraAgents**, which this repository must not edit. The framework change is therefore filed as `SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4` and this item tracks the documentation plus the verification of that change.
- **The advance is on stdout.** `engine:sync` logs `core updated <from> → <to>` to stdout, while the build-failure comment currently posts only `stderr[:500]` — so the failure path can name both SHAs without any change to `engine-sync.mjs`.
- **"If the behaviour is kept"** in draft AC2 is read as: the sync-at-build-time behaviour is kept (Option A/C), so the limitation note is a firm deliverable.

The plan below still holds; **no new children were needed**. This pass refreshed it against
the changed world (the framework item landed) and advanced the stage to `plan_complete`.

# Activity log source — feed the Activity Log from the Game Events channel

## Problem statement

The Activity Log is populated by roughly 102 direct `addLog(...)` / `activityLog.push` call sites spread across 19 source files and is **not** derived from the "Game Events" feed (`GameEventEmitter` → `PhaserEventBridge` / `__GAME_EVENTS__` / `GlobalEventBuffer` / debug overlay). The item asks for that check and, if true, for the log to be fed from the Game Events channel so the two cannot drift.

## Users

- **Player** — reads the Activity Log as the game's single narrative record; it must keep showing exactly the same rows, in the same order, with the same colours.
- **Developer / designer** — watches the dev "Game Events" overlay while playing and expects it to explain every log row (one source of truth, no second logging path to remember).
- **Developer / QA** — debugs via the event feed and replay tooling; wants log production observable through the same typed channel as the rest of the game's events.

Example user stories:

- As a developer, I want the Activity Log to be produced from the Game Events feed so that there is one instrumentation channel to reason about and one place to hook for analytics/replay.
- As a player, I want the log's wording, order and colours unchanged so that this internal change is invisible to me.
- As a QA engineer, I want to see each Activity Log row appear in the Game Events overlay so I can confirm nothing is logged outside the feed.

## Acceptance Criteria

> Confirmed — **Q2 option A** (instrument the existing log through the feed). Producer answered A in the /plan interview on 2026-11-05 (see Appendix).

- **Investigation recorded:** the work item states, with evidence, that activity-log rows are written directly by ~102 call sites across 19 files and **not** by the Game Events feed, which today carries only `card:placed` and `income-gained` from game code (plus engine `state-settled`).
- **Single write path:** every activity-log row is produced by a subscriber to a typed `activity-log` Game Events event that `addLog(...)` emits; a guard test fails if `state.activityLog` is written anywhere else.
- **Behaviour preserved:** each existing call site yields an identical entry (turn / text / type / seat fields) in the same order — regression test across purchase, sell, income, incident, loan, storyline and per-turn net rows.
- **Feed parity:** the dev "Game Events" overlay and `GlobalEventBuffer` show one `activity-log` event per log row in emission order; headless runs with no emitter attached still log every row and throw nothing.
- **Undo/redo and save/load** round-trips preserve the log exactly as today (regression tests for both).
- **Automated tests** cover the event contract, the single-writer guard, the no-emitter headless fallback, and overlay/buffer parity; the existing activity-log suites continue to pass.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the relevant docs (`docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` § Activity Log, event/telemetry docs).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No player-visible change:** log text, order, colours, seat prefixes, deferred-render ordering (`logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`, MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2), auto-scroll/no-yank and the scene-creation reset (MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6) are all unchanged.
- **Engine purity:** the engine modules that log today receive only `MainStreetState` — they must keep working with no scene and no emitter (headless Monte Carlo, unit tests, tutorial scenario).
- **No new global:** reuse the per-scene `GameEventEmitter` (`window.__GAME_EVENTS__`) and `GameEventMap` interface augmentation; no second emitter or module-level singleton event bus.
- **The log stays authoritative for undo and saves:** `state.activityLog` remains the record snapshotted by `MarketActionSnapshot` and serialised by `MainStreetStateSerialize`; no event-log persistence or replay reconstruction is introduced.
- **No performance regression:** emission must be O(1) per logged row with no per-frame work and no unbounded retention in production.
- **Scope boundary:** filtering and full seat attribution are owned by **MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW (Improved activity log)** — this item must not re-implement them.

## Existing state

- `MainStreetState.activityLog: LogEntry[]` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`) — each entry is `{ turn, text, type, seatId?, seatLabel?, seatColour? }` with `type` in `gain | loss | neutral | turn-header`.
- **Write sites:** 102 (definition plus calls) in 19 files — `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` (the `addLog` overloads), `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`, `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts`, `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts`, `src/TutorialScenario.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`.
- **The only "Game Events feed":** `GameEventEmitter` is created per scene in `core/src/ui/CardGameScene.ts:210` (`initEventSystem`), forwarded to Phaser by `PhaserEventBridge`, exposed as `window.__GAME_EVENTS__`, optionally mirrored into `GlobalEventBuffer` (DEV only) and rendered by the dev "Game Events" overlay (`core/src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts`).
- **Feed coverage is sparse and payload-light:** game code emits only `card:placed` (10 sites, payload `{ cardId, slotIndex }`) and `income-gained` (1 site, `{ amount }`); the engine emits `state-settled`. None carries the rich text the log displays (e.g. "Sold Cafe from slot 3 for +120 coins (+120 coins, no rep)").
- **The feed is not reachable from the logging code:** engine functions take `MainStreetState` only; the emitter lives on the scene (`CardGameScene.gameEvents`), so a feed-driven log needs either a state-level sink or a scene-level subscriber.
- **The log is state, not telemetry:** it is captured/restored by `MarketActionSnapshot` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`) and serialised by `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, so any change to how it is written must survive undo/redo and save/load.
- **Rendering:** `refreshLog()` in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` renders `state.activityLog`; it is untouched by this item.
- **Docs:** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` § "Activity Log (Effective Deltas and Per-Turn Net)" documents the log's content; `docs/dev/prd-milestone-1.md` § 11 documents the (largely unimplemented) telemetry event table — both are stale w.r.t. the current feed and must be reconciled.

**Finding: the Activity Log is not pulling its content from the Game Events feed.** It is written directly at each call site.

## Desired change

Implement option A (confirmed by the producer, 2026-11-05 — see Appendix Q2):

1. Declare a typed `activity-log` event in the Main Street `GameEventMap` augmentation, carrying the entry (`turn`, `text`, `type`, optional seat fields) and any source context needed for the overlay.
2. Make `addLog(...)` publish that event through the Game Events channel and make a **single subscriber** the only writer of `state.activityLog` — no other `push` remains.
3. Provide the no-emitter fallback so pure-engine/headless paths (Monte Carlo, unit tests, tutorial scenario) still append directly when no channel is attached.
4. Keep undo/redo and save/load semantics unchanged (the log stays the snapshot/serialised record).
5. Add the guard test, parity tests and docs updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` — `addLog` overloads become the event publisher; the single subscriber that appends to `state.activityLog`; headless fallback.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `LogEntry` / state-level sink field (`MainStreetState`) and the `activity-log` payload type.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — wire the sink/emitter when a new game state is created (and reset it on scene restart).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — attach the scene's `GameEventEmitter` to the log sink in `initEventSystem`/scene creation; detach on shutdown.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — undo/redo snapshots must stay consistent with the single-writer path.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — confirm serialisation/deserialisation of the log is unaffected.
- `core/src/core-engine/GameEventEmitter.ts` — only if the event map needs a housekeeping tweak (Main Street augmentation should live in `src/`).
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-feed.test.ts` — event contract, single-writer guard, headless fallback, ordering/parity.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-feed.browser.test.ts` — overlay/buffer parity and unchanged rendering.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — Activity Log section: the log is feed-driven; headless fallback note.
- `docs/dev/prd-milestone-1.md` — reconcile § 11 telemetry table with the events actually emitted.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Emitter reachability is the top risk.** The 102 write sites live in pure engine functions that receive only `MainStreetState`. Mitigation: attach a narrow sink (a callback, not the emitter) to state — but it must not break `safeClone`/serialisation/undo snapshots and must be cleared on scene teardown.
- **Re-entrancy / double-write.** If `addLog` both pushes and emits while a subscriber also pushes, rows double. Mitigation: exactly one writer, pinned by the guard test.
- **Undo divergence.** Undo restores the log from a snapshot but cannot retract emitted events, so the feed keeps the undone row. Mitigation: document that the feed is an append-only session audit trail and the log is the authoritative, undoable record (assumption below).
- **Headless regressions.** Monte Carlo (200 seeds) and tutorial paths must not throw or slow down without an emitter. Mitigation: explicit fallback plus a headless test and a timing sanity check.
- **Scope creep risk.** Making the feed user-facing, persisting events, replay reconstruction, analytics export, and re-doing seat attribution/filtering (MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW) are **out of scope** — record them as linked work items rather than widening this item.
- **Assumption (confirmed Q1, 2026-11-05):** "Game Events feed" means the scene `GameEventEmitter` feed surfaced by the dev "Game Events" overlay.
- **Assumption (confirmed Q2, 2026-11-05):** the log stays the persisted/undoable record; the feed is a runtime channel (option A), not the new source of truth.
- **Assumption (confirmed Q3, 2026-11-05):** this item is sequenced after MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW (Blocked-by dependency edge recorded) so the same call sites are edited once.

## Related work

- **MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW** — Improved activity log (in progress, `intake_complete`): adds per-seat attribution across every action path and presentation-only filters. Touches the same write sites; **ordering decided (Q3A, 2026-11-05): this item is Blocked-by it.**
- **MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF** — Identify different AI players (completed): seat label/colour prefix foundation in `addLog`.
- **MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2** — Activity Log should not show log line until the results have been shown in the UI (completed): deferred-render contract that must not regress.
- **MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6** — Turn log no longer displays (completed): scene-creation reset contract.
- **MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9** — Restore Activity Log rendering (completed): `refreshLog` deferral gate and re-render trigger.
- **MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV** — per-turn stat history (completed): keeps the graph series separate from the free-text log — precedent for "the log is not the analytics channel".
- Related docs: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Activity Log), `docs/dev/prd-milestone-1.md` (§ 11 Telemetry Events), `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (§ Activity log seat prefixes).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

**Status: all 3 producer decisions answered (2026-11-05, interactive /plan interview) — no open questions remain.**

### Q1 — What is the "Game Events feed"?

**Question:** The only event feed in the codebase is the per-scene `GameEventEmitter` (`core/src/ui/CardGameScene.ts`), shown by the dev **Game Events** overlay (`core/src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts`) and mirrored into `GlobalEventBuffer`. Is that the feed this item means, or a different intended feed (design doc, future user-facing panel, external telemetry)?

- **(A) The scene `GameEventEmitter` feed (debug overlay / `__GAME_EVENTS__`).** *(Recommended — it is the only "Game Events" feed that exists today; grep for "Game Events" resolves to that overlay.)*
- **(B) A different feed** — specify it (path/doc/name).

**Recommended:** (A) — the searchable codebase has exactly one "Game Events" feed, so this is the only actionable interpretation.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): (A) — the scene `GameEventEmitter` feed (debug overlay / `__GAME_EVENTS__`).** Source: interactive /plan interview reply.

### Q2 — How far should the log become feed-driven?

**Question:** Today the log is written directly at ~102 sites with rich, already-formatted text; the feed carries only `card:placed` and `income-gained` with payloads too thin to reconstruct log text. Which target do you want?

- **(A) Instrument the log into the feed (single write path, no behaviour change).** `addLog(...)` emits a typed `activity-log` event; one subscriber writes `state.activityLog`. Text/order unchanged; the overlay shows every log row. *(Recommended — smallest safe change, achieves "content comes from the feed" without rewriting 102 message strings.)*
- **(B) Full projection — rebuild log text from granular gameplay events.** Extend gameplay events (`card:placed`, purchases, income, incidents, loans, storyline…) with richer payloads and format log rows in a subscriber; retire `addLog`. Largest change; risks text/order regressions and loss of detail.
- **(C) Verification only — confirm and document that direct logging is intended.** Close with a documented finding, no code change.

**Recommended:** (A) — the log already has a rich, tested text contract; making the feed the transport gets the observability benefit without a high-risk rewrite.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): (A) — instrument the log into the feed (single write path, no behaviour change).** Source: interactive /plan interview reply. The ACs above are therefore final as drafted.

### Q3 — Ordering against "Improved activity log" (MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW)

**Question:** That item is at `intake_complete` and will edit the same ~102 call sites to add full seat attribution plus log filters. Should this item land after it, before it, or independently?

- **(A) After — record `Blocked-by: MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW`.** Land the attribution/filter work first, then funnel writes through the feed once. *(Recommended — avoids editing the same call sites twice and re-testing attribution under a new write path.)*
- **(B) Before — make this a prerequisite of MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW** (attribution is then added to the funnel).
- **(C) Independent — no dependency;** accept merge conflicts/rework in the same files.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): (A) — land after MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW; Blocked-by `MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW` dependency edge recorded.** Source: interactive /plan interview reply.

### Research summary

- Located the only event feed: `core/src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` `initEventSystem` (emitter, `PhaserEventBridge`, `window.__GAME_EVENTS__`, DEV-only `GlobalEventBuffer`), rendered by `core/src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts` (debug-tool label **Game Events**).

# Notify when loan is paid off

## Problem statement

Retiring a bank loan is currently silent in the UI: the closing writes one
`loss` activity-log row (`… loan repaid in full …`) and the HUD's loan line
simply disappears, but nothing acknowledges the milestone. A player can easily
miss that the debt is gone and that the weekly deduction has stopped.

## Users

- **Single-player player** (primary): the only seat with UI in single-player.
- **Human seat in competitive play**: the seat whose own loan retired.
- **AI seats / headless simulations**: no notification (no UI to show it to).

User stories:

- As a player making the final instalment, I want a congratulatory dialog so
  that I know the loan is fully repaid and I no longer owe the weekly
  deduction.
- As a player, I want the dialog to tell me the amount freed each week (and the
  total repaid) so I can plan the next few turns.
- As the human seat in a competitive run, I want the dialog only for my own
  payoff — not for an AI seat's.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The end-of-turn closing reports each loan retired by its final scheduled
   repayment as structured data on `TurnResult` (owning seat, per-turn
   repayment, total repayment, term), so presentation reacts to the engine's
   own decision instead of diffing `state.loans` before/after.
2. In single-player exactly one congratulatory dialog is presented per retired
   loan, and a later loan (taken and repaid again) produces exactly one more —
   the notification is per payoff, never per turn and never duplicated on a
   resumed/deferred closing.
3. Sequencing (producer Q1 = A): the dialog appears as its own modal immediately
   after the end-of-turn closing animations, and dismissing it continues into
   the End of Turn summary (or, where that gate is skipped, the normal
   next-week flow) exactly as it would have run without the dialog.
4. The dialog states that the player is debt free, the weekly amount no longer
   deducted, and the total repaid over the term; its copy lives once in a
   Phaser-free model so the text is testable without a browser.
5. The dialog follows the project's overlay conventions (instant appearance,
   reduced-motion safe, single dismiss action that resumes exactly the flow it
   interrupted) and never presents in `replayMode` / headless runs.
6. Competitive play presents the dialog for the human seat only, gated through
   the existing `isHumanSeatCredit` seam (producer Q3 = A); an AI seat's payoff
   changes nothing visible for the player.
7. A closing that ends the run in the same turn presents the game-over overlay
   instead — a congratulation never hides a loss or a win summary.
8. `loansEnabled: false` and no-loan turns stay byte-identical (no wallet, log,
   ledger or RNG change); the new `TurnResult` field defaults to empty and is
   never persisted, so save/load compatibility is unchanged.
9. Tests: unit tests for the payoff reporting, the copy model and the seat /
   replay gating; a browser test for the rendered dialog and its dismissal;
   documentation tests updated where the prose is pinned.
10. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
    comments, `README`, and the relevant `docs/` entries
    (`docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §5.1 and
    `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`).
11. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Presentation-only change: the repayment arithmetic, wallet debit and
  activity log stay exactly as they are today; no new state mutation and no
  new RNG consumption.
- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices; matches
  `MainStreetLoanOverlay`): `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`
  from `@ui`, every element parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths
  199/200/201, tracked in `s.overlayObjects`, SFX through `safePlaySound`,
  instant appearance (no fade-in).
- No new persisted save field — the payoff signal is transient.
- One modal at a time: the notification must not appear behind or on top of the
  End of Turn summary in a way that lets summary buttons be pressed.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the release pipeline and is out of scope.

## Existing state

- `applyLoanRepayments()` (`src/MainStreetLoans.ts`) debits, decrements and
  removes a retired loan, returning only the signed coin total
  (`number`). It already writes the "loan repaid in full" log row, so the
  retirement point is unambiguous.
- `TurnResult` (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`) carries per-turn presentation
  signals such as `newlyCompletedChallenges`, `pendingLoanOffer` and
  `choicePending`, which is the established engine → scene channel.
- End of turn: `applyLoanRepayments` runs in the closing
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`), and the competitive closing calls it
  from `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`.
- Presentation: `presentTurnSummaryGate()` and
  `completeDeferredClosingTail()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`)
  decide what is shown and what runs on dismissal; dialogs are rendered by
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` (which delegates to
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` for the loan dialogs).
- The HUD loan line (`src/scenes/MainStreetLoanRowModel.ts` consumers) already
  disappears on payoff; nothing congratulates.
- Human-vs-AI gating already exists as `isHumanSeatCredit()`
  (`src/MainStreetChallenges.ts`) and is used by the challenge celebration.

## Desired change

1. Give `applyLoanRepayments()` an out-channel (e.g. an optional `retiredOut`
   collection, or a returned report instead of a bare number) that records each
   retired loan's seat, per-turn repayment, total repayment and term, without
   changing its coin return value or its `apply: false` /
   `excludeOwnerIds` behaviour.
2. Surface the collected payoffs on `TurnResult` as a new optional
   seat-tagged array, populated by both the single-player and competitive
   closings (empty/absent when nothing retired).
3. Add a Phaser-free `MainStreetLoanPayoffModel` that turns a `TurnResult`
   payoff entry plus the seat context into the dialog copy: headline, "debt
   free" congratulation, weekly amount no longer deducted (`110 coins/week`)
   and total repaid over the term (`660 coins over 6 weeks`) — the same figures
   the HUD loan line and the loan dialogs already use (producer Q2 = B).
4. Render the dialog from the scene turn-flow immediately after the closing
   animations and ahead of the End of Turn summary (producer Q1 = A), once per
   payoff, with a single dismiss action that then presents the summary (or
   continues the next-week flow); suppressed in `replayMode` and for non-human
   seats.
5. Document the behaviour in the rules and UX docs, with the pinned-prose doc
   tests updated alongside.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — retire-report out-channel on
  `applyLoanRepayments()`; the payoff data model.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — new optional seat-tagged payoff field on
  `TurnResult` (and its docs).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — populate the field from the
  single-player/shared closing.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — populate the field from the
  competitive closing.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanPayoffModel.ts` — **new**, Phaser-free copy model
  + seat gating.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanPayoffOverlay.ts` — **new**, or an added mode in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts`; the overlay renderer.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — expose
  `showLoanPayoffDialog()` alongside the other dialogs.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — delegate the new dialog method.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — present the dialog at the
  agreed point in the closing → summary → next-turn sequence.
- `tests/main-street/loan-payoff-notification.test.ts` — **new**, engine

# Colour of service businesses

## Problem statement

Service businesses render in a dark purple that is visually indistinguishable
from the flat purple face used by every upgrade card, so the two card families
read as the same thing at a glance on the street and in hand. At the same
time, an upgrade card carries no information about *what* it upgrades: all 39
upgrade cards share one uniform purple face regardless of the business they
apply to.

## Users

- **Main Street player** (primary) — scanning their hand and the market needs
  to distinguish a service business from an upgrade card instantly, and to see
  which family of business an upgrade belongs to without reading its title.
  - *As a player, I want service businesses in a colour no other card family
    uses, so I never mistake a service business for an upgrade card.*
  - *As a player, I want each upgrade card to show the colour of the business
    family it upgrades, so I can pick a relevant upgrade from my hand without
    reading every title.*

- **Colour-blind player** — the distinction must not rely on hue alone; the
  checkered pattern is itself a non-colour cue, and the upgrade card keeps its
  title and "for <Business>" target text.

## Existing state

- Synergy-type card faces are coloured from two parallel palettes:
  `CARD_FACE_PALETTE` (dark faces, `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and the
  bright `synergyColor` accent palette. The static Node generator
  (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) duplicates both; an
  existing test asserts the two copies of the face palette agree
  (MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4).
- Service currently holds dark purple `#6A1B9A` (face) / `0x9B59B6` (accent).
- Upgrade cards are flat purple: background `#6B4C9A`, accent `#9B59B6`,
  rendered by `generateUpgradeCardSvg` / `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and by
  `cardColorScheme` / the family branch in the `.mjs` generator.
- 39 upgrade rows in `src/card-data.csv` carry a `targetBusiness` name but no
  synergy column of their own; synergy must be resolved by looking the target
  name up among business **and** community-space rows (6 targets are community
  spaces: Community Garden, Health Kiosk, Library, Park, Playground, Town
  Fountain).
- 9 businesses are bridge cards with two synergy types; 11 upgrade rows target
  them (Cafe, Food Truck, Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga
  Studio, Teahouse).

## Desired change

1. **New service colour.** Replace Service's palette entries with a pink /
   magenta that no other synergy type uses, in **both** palettes (face and
   accent) and in **both** copies (TypeScript and the `.mjs` duplicate), so the
   palette-agreement test still passes.
2. **Checkered upgrade faces.** Upgrade card faces become a checkerboard of
   violet and the synergy colour of the business the upgrade targets, instead
   of the current flat purple.
3. **Bridge targets use both colours.** When the upgrade targets a card with
   two synergy types, the checkerboard uses both synergy colours (with violet
   in the remaining squares).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Service synergy type's face colour is a pink/magenta distinct from
      every other synergy colour, applied in `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`
      (`src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and its `.mjs` duplicate
      (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`); the existing
      TS/mjs palette-agreement test passes unchanged in intent.
- [ ] The bright Service accent colour (`synergyColor`) is updated to the
      matching pink/magenta family so icons, header tint and art backing stay
      consistent (the `expanded-card-pool` assertion is updated to the new
      value).
- [ ] A generated upgrade card face renders as a checkerboard of violet and
      the target's synergy colour, for both the runtime generator
      (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` / `generateUpgradeCardSvg`) and the static
      `.mjs` generator, with both paths producing the same pattern.
- [ ] An upgrade targeting a single-synergy business yields a two-colour
      checkerboard (violet + that synergy colour).
- [ ] An upgrade targeting a bridge business (two synergy types) yields all
      three colours: violet plus **both** synergy colours.
- [ ] An upgrade whose target synergy cannot be resolved (unknown or missing
      target) degrades safely to the existing flat purple face and never
      throws.
- [ ] Upgrade cards remain legible: title, "for <Business>" target text, cost
      badge and art stay readable over the checkerboard (existing contrast
      expectations in the SVG tests are preserved).
- [ ] New unit tests cover: the new service colour, single-synergy
      checkerboard, bridge-target three-colour checkerboard, unresolvable
      target fallback, and TS/mjs pattern agreement.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The static Node generator runs outside the TS build and cannot import
  TypeScript modules, so any palette or resolver change must be duplicated
  there and kept in agreement (existing project pattern).
- Upgrade synergy colour must be **derived**, not added as a new CSV column:
  `targetBusiness` is the only link today, and adding data columns would
  invalidate CSV checksums and pack fixtures.
- Upgrade **card** faces change only. The in-game board upgrade accent (the
  gold corner shard on an upgraded business, `UpgradeOverlaySpec`) and the
  owner-coloured seat border are out of scope — they are a separate visual
  language and were deliberately settled by MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF.
- Card faces must remain readable at the reduced hand/stacked scale (the art
  zone and text column must not be masked by the pattern).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — new Service entry in `synergyColor` and
  `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`; likely the natural home for a pure
  `upgradeFaceBackground(targetSynergyTypes)`-style resolver.
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — duplicated palettes plus
  the `upgrade` family branch in `cardColorScheme`; mirror the checkerboard and
  the new service colour.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `generateUpgradeCardSvg`,
  `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` (upgrade branch) and `cardColorScheme`; emit the
  checkerboard rect group (mirroring the existing `cardFaceSplitSvg` approach,
  possibly generalised into a checker tile helper).
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` — re-export any new resolver alongside
  `cardFaceBackground`.
- `src/card-data.csv` — read-only reference: `targetBusiness` values are the
  lookup keys; no schema change expected.
- `tests/main-street/mjs-svg-generator.test.ts` — palette-agreement and static
  render-path tests; extend for the checkerboard.
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — runtime SVG generator tests;
  add upgrade-face cases.
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — asserts the Service accent
  value; update to the new colour.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4 — Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge
  cards)** (completed) — established `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`, `cardFaceBackground`
  and the TS/mjs palette-agreement test this item builds on.
- **MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF — Identify different AI players** (completed) — moved
  upgrade state to the owner-coloured border + top-left accent; constrains the
  board visual language this item must not disturb.
- **MS-0MVZC5V6L001OOXN — Upgrade highlights should only be the current
  player's businesses** (completed) — upgrade targeting/placement rendering;
  related to how upgrade cards are presented.
- **MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38 — shader-style upgrade accent remediation** — the
  board-level gold upgrade shard; explicitly out of scope here (Q2 = A).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: palette collision.** Pink must be checked against the seat-colour
  palette (`MainStreetSeatColours`) — seat colours identify *owners*, synergy
  colours identify *card families*; a near-identical pink could blur that.
  Mitigation: pick a pink distinguishable from the seat palette and note the
  choice in comments.
- **Risk: legibility at small scale.** A checkerboard under the 64×64 art zone
  and the text column may reduce contrast. Mitigation: keep the pattern
  behind the existing translucent overlays, keep tile contrast modest, and
  assert legibility in the SVG tests.
- **Risk: colour as sole cue.** Mitigation: the pattern itself is a non-colour
  cue, and the title plus "for <Business>" line remain.
- **Risk: two copy drift.** The TS and `.mjs` generators can diverge silently.
  Mitigation: extend the existing agreement test to the checkerboard geometry
  and colours.
- **Risk: scope creep.** A general "cards show their family colour" refactor,
  a redesign of the board upgrade accent, or adding a `targetSynergy` CSV
  column are all out of scope — record as separate work items if raised.
- **Assumption:** "violet" for the retained checkerboard colour means the
  existing upgrade family purple (`#6B4C9A`); the request says
  "the current colour and the colour of the type of business they upgrade".
- **Assumption:** bridge targets show both synergy colours because the
  producer explicitly chose option B in the intake interview.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which colour should Service businesses become?** (asked because the
  brief said "change the service business" without naming a colour) —
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **(a) Pink/magenta** (`#AD1457` /
  `#C2185B` family), chosen to be distinct from every other synergy hue.

- **Q: Where should the checkered upgrade pattern apply?** — Answer (producer,
  interactive reply): **(a) Upgrade card faces only** — the market/hand card
  face changes; the in-game board upgrade accent stays as-is.

- **Q: For upgrades targeting a bridge business with two synergy types, which
  colour does the checkerboard use?** — Answer (producer, interactive reply):
  **(b) Both colours** — the checkerboard uses violet plus both synergy
  colours.

- **Q: (research, no producer input needed) Do upgrade rows carry a synergy
  column?** — Answer: no; all 39 upgrade rows have an empty `targetSynergy`.
  Synergy must be resolved from `targetBusiness` against the business and
  community-space rows. Source: `src/card-data.csv`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0** – Allow drag and drop of upgrades from hand to card (completed)
- **MS-0MVZC5V6L001OOXN** – Upgarde highlights should only be the current players businesses (completed)
- **MS-0MV5VOIV40020KXT** – Smarter AI hand acquisition: gate expensive businesses and untargeted upgrades (completed)

# Turn summary dialog suppressed by reduced motion setting

Discovered from: MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (End of Turn summary) / MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT (dialog overlay).

## Problem

The Turn Summary dialog (MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT) never appears for a player with the
reduced-motion setting enabled, even though the dialog itself is instant-appearance
(no fade, no tween) and therefore reduced-motion safe. The closing silently
auto-advances instead of pausing on the summary.

## Root Cause — two separate reduced-motion gates

1. **Display gate.** `shouldGateTurnSummary` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, ~line 544)
   returns `false` when `settingsPanel.reducedMotion === true`, so the dialog is never presented:

   ```ts
   if (s.replayMode === true) return false;
   if (s.settingsPanel?.reducedMotion === true) return false;   // <-- culprit
   ```

2. **Path gate (deeper).** Even if gate 1 is removed the dialog still cannot appear, because
   reduced motion never takes the deferred-closing path that the dialog gates. In `endTurn`
   (`MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, ~line 229):

   ```ts
   const deferred = !inTutorialBefore && !reducedMotion && !s.replayMode;
   ...
   result = processEndOfTurn(s.state, deferred ? { deferResourceApplication: true } : undefined);
   ```

   The engine only sets `requiresDeferredClosing: true` when `deferResourceApplication` is
   passed (`MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, ~line 776). `shouldGateTurnSummary`'s first
   guard is `if (result.requiresDeferredClosing !== true) return false;`, so a reduced-motion
   closing has no deferred result and the gate is a no-op — the immediate path advances the
   day with no dialog. Removing only the display gate would therefore change nothing.

## Fix

Both need to change so that reduced motion is honoured by *animations* but not by the
*dialog*:

1. Remove the `reducedMotion === true` early return from `shouldGateTurnSummary`
   (keep replay / tutorial / competitive guards).
2. Let reduced motion take the deferred-closing path in `endTurn`, so
   `requiresDeferredClosing` is set and the gate has something to gate (keep tutorial and
   replay on their existing immediate paths). The reduced-motion animator already finalizes
   its income/incident presentation without tweens, so the deferred closing completes
   promptly; `deferUntilIncomeCollected` stays bounded so the closing can never hang.

Design note: with reduced motion the phased income show still schedules its
`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS` (2.2 s) phase slots before the collect step runs, so the summary may
appear up to ~2.2 s × number of non-empty phases later. Confirm that pacing is acceptable,
or skip the empty-phase time in reduced motion, so the dialog does not feel like a hang.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A reduced-motion single-player `endTurn` produces a result with
   `requiresDeferredClosing === true` and `shouldGateTurnSummary` returns `true`.
2. The Turn Summary dialog is presented for reduced-motion players, and `[ Next Turn ]`
   resumes the deferred closing exactly once (day advances, HUD shows post-delta values).
3. Existing guards still suppress the dialog for replay, tutorial and competitive closings.
4. The dialog stays instant-appearance (no fade/tween) and plays SFX via `safePlaySound`
   (mute respected); no new animation is introduced for reduced motion.
5. Unit tests cover the guard matrix (reduced motion on/off × replay × tutorial ×
   competitive) and the `endTurn` deferred-path selection under reduced motion; a browser
   test asserts the dialog appears after a reduced-motion end-of-turn.
6. Changed-scope test gate passes; the dev-push gate (full suite) passes before merge.

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R** – Gating: wire turn summary into finishTurnPresentation (completed)
- **MS-0MVRNV9Y8008IKGK** – Competitive summary rows end-to-end (open)
